//overrides: expo-random — prunes an Expo/React Native toolchain that a browser-only app
can never run or ship.
Chain: fhirclient -> isomorphic-webcrypto -> expo-random. isomorphic-webcrypto
requests `expo-random: "*"`; expo-random >= 13 declares a peerDependency on
`expo: "*"`, and npm 7+ auto-installs peers, so `npm install` was pulling in
expo, @expo/cli and metro. expo-random@11.0.0 is the newest release with no
peerDependencies (deps: base64-js only), so pinning it cuts that subtree.
Safe because the code path never executes. fhirclient's browser entry reaches
isomorphic-webcrypto only via `globalThis.crypto ? globalThis.crypto :
require('isomorphic-webcrypto')` (lib/security/browser.js) — a require inside
a ternary, so it is neither evaluated in a browser (globalThis.crypto always
exists) nor statically bundled by Rollup. Verified: the dist chunks are
byte-identical before and after this override, and contain zero react-native
or isomorphic-webcrypto references.
Measured effect: node_modules 562 MB -> 438 MB, lockfile 1179 -> 895 packages,
npm audit 28 -> 14 advisories.
NOT fully pruned: react-native itself (~149 MB with @react-native/* and
react-devtools-core) still arrives via isomorphic-webcrypto ->
react-native-securerandom, which declares a hard `react-native: "*"` peer in
every published version, so no version pin removes it. It accounts for 2 of
the 14 remaining advisories (shell-quote, ws). Removing it needs a blunter
tool — `omit=peer` in .npmrc, or aliasing react-native to a stub — judged not
worth the maintenance surprise. The other 12 advisories come from real
devDependencies (fsh-sushi, stylelint, eslint, @formbox/renderer).
Revisit if fhirclient 3.x (beta as of 2026-07) drops isomorphic-webcrypto, or
if anything here ever needs to run under React Native.
